utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Madam Registrar. And good afternoon to you all. Could we call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. All the accused are here. Prosecution is Mr. McCloskey and Ms. Janisiewicz. I just wanted to start with that, not to make mistakes. Oh, she's not here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She is not here. Okay. So you are all alone today. Thank you, Mr. McCloskey. And from the Defence teams I only notice the absence of Mr. Ostojic. That's it. Can we bring in the witness, please? And we go into closed session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you wish to address the Chamber first, Mr. Haynes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I will. The lady with the Polish name who has been very accurate about the length of Mr. McCloskey's examination-in-chief so far estimated to me that he will probably take one more session, and I think it would be nice if Mr. McCloskey would give us a fairly -- as good an estimate as he can as to that. At the end of the examination-in-chief, I think it would be appropriate to take a break. I think I will go first. And it's likely that we'll have to make certain physical arrangements within the courtroom before I can begin asking the witness any questions. I don't want to make any secret of it. We've got some big maps and various other media to show to him which will need to be affixed to boards and things before he can start. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: So that's really all I want to contribute. It may well be that between ourselves we change that and somebody whose estimate for cross-examination of this witness is much shorter would prefer to begin and finish tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But we will know that when we know how long Mr. McCloskey is going to be and we'll take it from there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Haynes. Let's start with you, Mr. McCloskey. How much more time you think you require for -- to finish the examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, to give Ms. Janisiewicz a name, that may be about right. These some 25 intercepts, as you can tell, it's sometimes give to gauge how long a witness is going to speak, but they are going to be fairly pointed. So I don't think we are going to want or allow narratives, but again that's hard to tell. I also, in looking at my outline, I want him to identify the logbooks that he took from Mali Zvornik so that's clear, describe a little bit about what they are, but I don't have an intention for him to go through them at length.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So would one session be enough for you tomorrow or do you think you need more?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I may be lucky to do it in one session but it might be one and a part of a session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Though it's hard to tell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Granted that the witness hasn't finished the examination-in-chief, Mr. Zivanovic, as the matters stand now, how long do you think -- you had asked for five years?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you require five hours?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Meek, you had asked for three hours, almost four hours, 3 hours 50 minutes. I don't know what made you deduct those ten minutes to be honest with you, but do you still require the same time?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, actually I'll probably require more time than what I put down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Eight hours, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You still require eight hours, yeah, okay. Mr. Stojanovic? You asked for two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we will probably need less time. After having seen the documents, maybe up to an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Ms. Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think I might need more time, three hours and a half, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Josse or Mr. Krgovic, you asked for 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Absolute maximum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So would you be prepared to take over tomorrow after ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Absolutely pointless, Your Honour. First of all, Mr. Krgovic is in fact going to cross-examine the witness, but there is every prospect that we will have no questions. It would be absolutely pointless us going first frankly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And you asked for 12 hours, Mr. Haynes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes. I think I'll probably be about as long as Mr. McCloskey with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. So we'll take that up tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honour, in fact the reason I dealt with this is I wanted to mention one other thing, and this is really in fairness to Mr. Thayer. He, I know, wants to raise an issue to do with General Smith and these various pleadings that the Chamber has in relation to whether he's going to be an expert witness. Mr. Thayer wrote to Ms. Fauveau and myself a week ago, asked if he could raise it on Monday, I explained that I wouldn't be here, and he very kindly agreed to postpone the matter. In fairness to him, I'm now raising the matter. I suspect he would like a few minutes tomorrow to canvass various matters prior to the break. Ms. Fauveau and I are both prepared to respond. I would invite the Chamber, if it's agreeable to hear any submissions on the subject to limit it to very few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. We were trying to fill in all the time actually. Mr. McCloskey? Thank you, Mr. Josse. Will Mr. Thayer be available tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. I think we have to sleep on all this, and -- yes, Mr. Haynes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: That's all been very helpful. There are of course one or two other outstanding legal issues that you've yet to come back to us on or you may require further input on. To borrow Mr. Josse's phrase, if we did go very far into a second session, I would frankly regard starting the cross-examination before weeks' break myself as pretty pointless because I don't think I could even get through any meaningful topic at all within an hour or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But I guessed that's what you meant in the first place. So ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I was just trying to see how the day was shaping up. If there were two hours left I would get on and start.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not possible for you to identify maybe some areas --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I shall look at them tonight, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Introductory ones that you could perhaps dispose of.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I leave it up to you, Mr. Haynes and then we discuss again tomorrow. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't have any objection to that. Perhaps having a week to look at it, the estimates may be below 31 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not that confident. So we stand adjourned to tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 28th day of September, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.57 p.m.,
